title: Quiet Utility — Braun Catalog Repose
description: A single-product introduction stripped to its bare essentials: one silhouette, one name, one sentence of function. Where other minimalist templates leave whitespace by accident, this one wields it as the primary design material.
philosophy: This template exists on the conviction that a well-made object needs no salesmanship. It refuses gradients, decorative geometry, and typographic hierarchy beyond three discreet sizes — because every added element is a vote of no-confidence in the product itself. It is built for the speaker who knows that silence in a room carries more authority than noise, and for an audience trained to read restraint as a quality signal. The Braun catalog did not ask for your attention; it assumed you were already paying it.
goodFor: Single hardware or consumer electronics product launch reveals to design-literate audiences
Industrial design portfolio reviews where the object must dominate
3-line product tagline slides that need at least 40% canvas to breathe
Model-generation comparisons using paired product silhouettes
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly business reviews with multiple overlapping data series
Team introduction slides requiring headshots, names, and role bios
Marketing decks that need color-coded feature comparison tables
Audiences expecting kinetic transitions or narrative visual storytelling
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide carries itself with the authority of a catalog page that never solicited attention — negative space is the primary material, not a byproduct of sparse content. A single product silhouette commands the right half with cool, archival precision while a hairline rule performs the only visible structural labor. The mood is warm-document stillness: industrial craft presented on a ground that reads as considered, not sterile. Avoid drop shadows, decorative marks, vignettes, or any secondary element that competes with the silhouette's quiet dominance.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with roughly 8% outer margin on all sides; no header band, no footer band except a catalog or deck identifier anchored flush-right in the bottom two columns. Product name sits flush-left in cols 2–7, positioned in the upper third of the vertical canvas at the largest of three permitted sizes, immediately followed by a single hairline rule spanning cols 2–10 — the slide's sole structural ornament. A one-line function descriptor in the smallest permitted size sits just below the rule, constrained to cols 2–6. Product silhouette occupies the right half of the canvas, cols 7–12, edge-cropped at the top and right margins, leaving the lower-left quadrant as deliberate, load-bearing void.

examples.promptCore: The slide reads like a Braun product catalog page pulled out of time — still, deliberate, quietly authoritative. The object owns the left half of the canvas; the right half offers only the minimum language needed to name what is already visible. Compositional tension comes from asymmetric weight, not from ornamentation — the ruled line does the work that color or decoration would do in lesser templates. Avoid any layered geometry, drop shadows, icon clusters, or gradient fields that would dilute the authority of the silhouette.

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1920 1080" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet">
  <rect width="1920" height="1080" fill="#f5f0e6"/>

  <!-- Product silhouette: cols 1-6, vertically centered, edge-kissing -->
  <!-- A restrained cylindrical radio/speaker form, centered around x=480, y=540 -->
  <g transform="translate(480 540)">
    <!-- Main body: rounded rectangular radio -->
    <rect x="-230" y="-300" width="460" height="600" rx="10" ry="10" fill="#1e1c1a"/>

    <circle cx="-80" cy="90" r="140" fill="none" stroke="#1e1c1a" stroke-width="1"/>

    <!-- Dial indicator -->

      <line x1="-16" y1="26" x2="-9" y2="19"/>

      <line x1="-144" y1="154" x2="-151" y2="161"/>

    <!-- Small secondary knob -->
    <circle cx="140" cy="90" r="45" fill="#f5f0e6"/>

  </g>

  <!-- Text block: cols 7-11, starts around x=1080 -->
  <g transform="translate(1080 440)">
    <!-- Single-pixel horizontal rule -->
    <line x1="0" y1="0" x2="280" y2="0" stroke="#1e1c1a" stroke-width="1"/>

    <text x="0" y="34" font-family="ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="13" fill="#7a7468" letter-spacing="4">FEATURE  —  03 / 08</text>

    <text x="0" y="200" font-family="Georgia, ui-serif, serif" font-size="22" fill="#1e1c1a" font-style="italic">
      <tspan x="0" dy="0">A single weighted dial traverses the entire reception band without</tspan>
      <tspan x="0" dy="36">detents or digital interruption, returning authority over frequency</tspan>
      <tspan x="0" dy="36">selection to the hand that operates the instrument.</tspan>
    </text>
  </g>

  <!-- Page number flush bottom-right -->
  <text x="1860" y="1020" font-family="ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="12" fill="#7a7468" text-anchor="end" letter-spacing="2">03</text>
  <text x="1860" y="1040" font-family="ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#7a7468" text-anchor="end" letter-spacing="2">QUIET UTILITY</text>
</svg>
examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid; product silhouette anchors cols 1–6 as a vertically centered, edge-kissing image with generous crop room top and bottom — no border, no shadow. Text block occupies cols 7–11: a single-pixel horizontal rule sits above the feature label, followed by the feature name, then a one-sentence descriptor below with extra leading. Page number sits flush bottom-right; no header band, no footer rule, no decorative frame of any kind.
